short: Word-level ECoG encoder-decoder; all changed components standard. 3% WER is on repeats of 50 sentences; unseen sentences and participants were never tested.
position: Makin et al. [@makin2020] changed the decoder (M06, encoder–decoder), output unit (M08, words), training-only targets (M02, MFCC) and training data (M03, transfer); all four are standard, none ahead: Krishna et al. [@krishna2019] trained an attention encoder–decoder on EEG seven months earlier, and Brain2Char [@sun2020] [concurrent], from the same lab, used the same MFCC loss. The protocol is strong: 30 models per condition paired on random held-out blocks, corrected tests, a noise control. The headline 3% WER comes from held-out repeats of the same 50 sentences; the cited 60% [@herff2015] came from held-out phrases, so the gap compares unlike tests. Unseen sentences and participants were never tested; on sentences never duplicated in training the reference is 23.8% WER with 125,000 words [@willett2023].
